mainTopic: Why כיבוד אב ואם and building the בית המקדש do not override even a light שבת לאו: they are only a הכשר מצוה, so the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה still stands.
overview: This amud asks where the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה really comes from, and why some cases seem to point the other way. First the גמרא says a father's order to his son was only the light שבת לאו of driving a loaded animal (מחמר), and even so כיבוד אב ואם does not override it. That raises a challenge: then maybe an עשה never overrides a לאו. Saying that שבת is stricter does not help, because a ברייתא applies the same verse to lighter prohibitions, like a כהן becoming טמא or not returning a lost object. The answer is that driving the animal is only a הכשר מצוה, a preparation, and not the מצוה itself. The גמרא then runs the same steps with the building of the בית המקדש on שבת and gives the same answer. Since the lesson about הכשר מצוה already comes from the father's case, the גמרא asks what the verse 'keep My שבתות and revere My מקדש' is for. It answers that the verse teaches the right kind of awe for the מקדש, by comparing it to keeping שבת, and that comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even the light prohibition of driving an animal is not overridden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. The case in the verse is the light לאו of מחמר, and even so כיבוד אב ואם does not push it aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is the prohibition of driving a loaded animal on שבת, and even so, honoring parents does not override it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the earlier reading that the father ordered a מלאכה carrying כרת. It says the father's order was only the light שבת לאו of driving a loaded animal, and even so the son may not listen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא tried to prove from the father's case that an עשה would override even a כרת prohibition if not for the verse. Here it answers that the case may be only the plain לאו of מחמר, which has no כרת, so no proof about כרת comes from it. But now כיבוד אב ואם fails to override even a plain לאו, which sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of driving a loaded animal on שבת. It is a plain לאו, with no כרת.
Does not push aside or override.
And even so.

phrases.english: It refers to the prohibition of driving a loaded animal,
and even so, it does not override it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו דִּמְחַמֵּר, וַאֲפִילּוּ הָכִי לָא דָּחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading, just before this section, that the father's order involved a מלאכה with כרת. That reading was used to prove that an עשה would otherwise override כרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כיבוד אב ואם does not override even the plain לאו of מחמר on שבת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from כיבוד אב ואם that an עשה would override a כרת prohibition.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as dealing only with the plain לאו of מחמר, not a כרת-level מלאכה.

steps.title: Why not learn that an עשה never overrides a לאו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה. Maybe this case should teach the opposite rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead of what we hold, that an עשה comes and overrides a לא תעשה, let us learn from here that it does not override!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. If כיבוד אב ואם cannot override even a light לאו, maybe we should learn from this that an עשה never overrides a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned עשה דוחה לא תעשה from one example, ציצית overriding כלאים, and spread it to every case. Here is an example that points the other way. So why build the rule on ציצית and not on כיבוד אב ואם?

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that a positive מצוה pushes aside a negative prohibition when the two clash.
That we hold as settled.
Let us learn from here.

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that עשה דוחה לא תעשה is wrong. It is testing the rule: why choose one example over the other?

phrases.english: Rather than what we hold,
that a positive commandment comes and overrides a prohibition,
phrases.notes: This is the rule we learned earlier from ציצית overriding כלאים.

phrases.english: let us learn from here that it does not override!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקַיְימָא לַן דְּאָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, לִיגְמַר מֵהָכָא דְּלָא לִידְחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 1 to attack the general rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The general rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כיבוד אב ואם, an עשה, does not override even a light לאו. That opposite example could serve as the model just as well as ציצית and כלאים.

steps.title: Maybe שבת prohibitions are special because they are stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible way out: every שבת לאו, even מחמר, may be stricter than other prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: the prohibitions of שבת are different, because they are severe —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer and is about to knock it down. Maybe the prohibitions of שבת are just stricter, so nothing general can be learned from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the light לאוין of שבת are stricter than ordinary ones, this case is a special exception. Then the general rule from ציצית still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It introduces a possible answer that will be rejected.
It is different.
Because they are severe or strict.

phrases.english: And if you say,
the prohibitions of Shabbat are different, because they are severe —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, שָׁאנֵי לָאוֵי דְּשַׁבָּת דַּחֲמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of the general rule against the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: Shabbat is a special exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of כיבוד אב ואם seemed to show that an עשה never overrides a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe it only shows that the לאוין of שבת are especially strict.

steps.title: The תנא treats all prohibitions the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that שבת is special. The תנא applies the verse to ordinary prohibitions and sees no problem in doing so.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא is talking about prohibitions in general, and he raises no difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 3. The תנא uses this verse for regular prohibitions, not only שבת, and never objects that שבת is stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the לאוין of שבת were stricter, the תנא could not apply the שבת verse to light prohibitions. Since he does so freely, שבת is not treated as special here. So the challenge from step 2 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Is talking about cases in general.
A sage of the משנה or ברייתא period.
Raises a difficulty or challenge.

phrases.english: But the tanna is talking about prohibitions in general,
and he raises no difficulty!
phrases.notes: Meaning, he never asks how a lesson about שבת, which is stricter, can apply to lighter rules.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא בְּעָלְמָא קָאֵי, וְלָא קָפָרֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the לאוין of שבת are special.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא applies the verse to ordinary prohibitions without any objection. So שבת is not treated as stricter in this matter.

steps.title: The ברייתא: do not obey a father who orders breaking any prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that backs up step 4. A son does not obey a father who tells him to become טמא or not to return a lost object, because everyone must honor הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One might think that if his father told him 'Become טמא,' or told him 'Do not return the lost object,' he should obey him. So the verse says: 'Each man shall fear his mother and his father, and you shall keep My Sabbaths.' All of you are obligated in My honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it relied on in step 4. The ברייתא uses the שבת verse to teach that you never obey a parent who tells you to break any prohibition, even a light one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming טמא as a כהן and not returning a lost object are ordinary prohibitions, not שבת ones. Yet the ברייתא learns them from 'and you shall keep My Sabbaths.' That proves the תנא does not treat the prohibitions of שבת as special. So the challenge stays strong: כיבוד אב ואם does not override any לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Become ritually impure, said for example to a son who is a כהן.
Do not return the lost object. This breaks the מצוה of השבת אבידה.
Therefore the verse says. It introduces the verse that settles the question.
All of you, parents and children alike, must honor Me.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא learns from ויקרא 19:3 that a parent's order to break any prohibition, light or severe, is not obeyed. That is why the גמרא cannot say שבת is a special case. So the question from step 2 is back: why don't we learn from כיבוד אב ואם that an עשה never overrides a לאו? The next step answers this.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice: a child must not obey a parent who tells him to break a prohibition, because the parent is also obligated in the honor of הקב״ה.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One might think, if his father said to him: Become impure,
phrases.notes: Picture a son who is a כהן, whose father asks him to become טמא, for example to fetch something from near a dead body.

phrases.english: or said to him: Do not return it,
phrases.notes: He means a lost object the son found and has to give back.

phrases.english: one might think he should obey him?
Therefore the verse says:
"Each man shall fear his mother and his father,
and you shall keep My Sabbaths",
all of you are obligated in My honor.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, יָכוֹל אָמַר לוֹ אָבִיו: הִיטַּמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 4 that the תנא speaks of prohibitions in general.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the תנא does not treat the prohibitions of שבת as stricter than others.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 19:3 that applies 'and you shall keep My Sabbaths' to טומאה and השבת אבידה.

steps.title: The father's case is only preparation for the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 2. Driving an animal for a parent is only a הכשר מצוה, so it cannot teach that a מצות עשה never overrides a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case really is מחמר. We still cannot learn from it that a positive מצוה does not override a prohibition, because the proof can be knocked down. Instructions like these are different, since they are only preparation for the מצוה, not the מצוה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the case of מחמר and explains why it does not break the rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה. Driving the animal is only a step before honoring the parent; it is not the actual honoring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 2 the challenge was this: if כיבוד אב ואם cannot push aside even the light לאו of מחמר, maybe a מצות עשה never pushes aside a לאו. The answer is that the son is not feeding or dressing his father while he drives the animal. It is only a הכשר מצוה, and a mere preparation is too weak to override a לאו, so this case teaches nothing about real מצוות.

keyTerms.meaning: to refute, to knock down a proof
preparation for a מצוה, not the מצוה itself
a positive commandment pushes aside a negative commandment

steps.whatToRemember: The rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה stands. A mere הכשר מצוה is too weak to override a לאו.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because there is a way to refute it:
phrases.notes: He means: we can't learn from the father's case that a מצות עשה never overrides a לאו, because that proof can be knocked down.

phrases.english: What about these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the father's instructions, like driving the loaded animal.

phrases.english: since they are only preparation for a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the idea that שבת is special in step 4, the גמרא gives a different answer to the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: this is preparation for a מצוה, not the מצוה itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father's case shows that a מצות עשה does not override a לא תעשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's case is only a הכשר מצוה, so it proves nothing about a real מצות עשה.

steps.title: A new possible source: building the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests we might have learned that a מצות עשה overrides even a prohibition with כרת from the building of the בית המקדש. It quotes a ברייתא about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you might have thought to learn it from building the בית המקדש. A ברייתא teaches: one might think building the בית המקדש overrides שבת. The פסוק says, "Keep My שבתות and revere My Sanctuary," which means all of you must honor Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is looking for where we might have gotten the idea that a מצות עשה can override even a severe prohibition with כרת. It brings a ברייתא about building the בית המקדש on שבת, and this sets up the inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that without a פסוק we might have thought the מצוה of building the בית המקדש pushes aside שבת. The פסוק teaches that it does not, because everyone, including the builders, must honor הקב״ה by keeping שבת. The next step will draw a conclusion from the fact that a פסוק was needed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: it would enter your mind to say (a possible first thought)
let it be derived
building the Holy Temple, which is a מצות עשה
one might have thought
the פסוק teaches us

phrases.english: Rather, it would have entered your mind to say:
Let it be learned from the building of the Temple.
phrases.notes: "It" is the idea that a מצות עשה overrides even a prohibition that carries כרת.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ דּוֹחֶה שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: One might think building the Temple overrides Shabbat.
So the verse says:
"You shall keep My Sabbaths
and revere My Sanctuary."
All of you are obligated in My honor.
phrases.notes: Even the people building the בית המקדש must honor הקב״ה by keeping שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: תֵּיתֵי מִבִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the discussion of כיבוד אב ואם, the גמרא proposes a new source for the possible thought that a מצות עשה overrides even a prohibition with כרת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offering a new source for the possible first thought.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No source has yet been found for the idea that a מצות עשה overrides a prohibition with כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא about building the בית המקדש might be that source.

steps.title: Without the verse, building would override Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as dealing with real מלאכות that carry כרת. Since a פסוק was needed to stop it, without the פסוק the מצוה would have overridden שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about building and demolishing, which are full מלאכות? The only reason building the בית המקדש does not override שבת is that the תורה wrote "Keep My שבתות." This implies that otherwise, it would override.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא. Because the תורה needed a special פסוק to stop the building on שבת, it seems that a מצות עשה would normally override even a prohibition with כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בונה and סותר are real מלאכות of שבת, and breaking them carries כרת. If a special פסוק was needed to say the בית המקדש building does not override them, then the default must be that a מצות עשה does override even such severe prohibitions. This would explain the possible first thought the גמרא was looking for.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not? (introduces a suggested reading)
building and demolishing, two מלאכות of שבת
the Merciful One, meaning הקב״ה in the תורה
but if it were not so

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final answer. The גמרא is only showing where the possible first thought could come from. The next step rejects this reading.

phrases.english: What, is it not about building and demolishing,
phrases.notes: These are full מלאכות of שבת, and breaking them carries כרת.

phrases.english: and the reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"You shall keep My Sabbaths";
but if not for that, it would override!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a מצות עשה would normally override even a prohibition with כרת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about building the בית המקדש: a special פסוק was needed to stop it from overriding שבת.

steps.title: The ברייתא is only about driving a loaded animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 8. The ברייתא is not about real מלאכות with כרת. It is about the ordinary prohibition of driving a loaded animal, and even so the building of the בית המקדש does not override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the prohibition of driving a loaded animal. Even so, the מצוה of building does not push it aside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 8. It says the ברייתא may be talking only about the light prohibition of driving an animal, not about מלאכות that carry כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 tried to prove that without the פסוק, building the מקדש would override even a כרת prohibition. Here the גמרא says the ברייתא could be about a plain לאו only. That removes the proof about כרת, and it also creates a new problem, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition of driving a loaded animal on שַׁבָּת
And even so
It does not override / push aside

phrases.english: No, it is the prohibition of driving a loaded animal,
phrases.notes: This is someone leading a loaded animal on שבת, which is a plain לאו and not one of the main מלאכות.

phrases.english: and even so, it does not override it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's reading that the ברייתא deals with כרת-level מלאכות.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that a מצות עשה would override a כרת prohibition
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as dealing only with the light לאו of driving an animal.

steps.title: Then learn that a מצות עשה never overrides a לאו
steps.stepSummary: If building the מקדש cannot override even the light לאו of driving an animal, we should learn from here that no עשה overrides a לאו. That contradicts the accepted rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we hold that an עשה comes and overrides a לא תעשה. Let us learn from here that it does not override!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 9. It warns that this reading seems to cancel the well-known rule that עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building the בית המקדש is a big מצות עשה. If it cannot even push aside a simple לאו, it looks like no עשה ever overrides a לאו. This is the same challenge the גמרא raised earlier in step 2, now coming back.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / it is established for us
A positive מִצְוָה comes and overrides a prohibition
Let us learn from here

phrases.english: But then, that which we hold
that a positive מצוה comes and overrides a prohibition,
let us learn from here that it does not override!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא דְּקַיְימָא לַן דְּאָתֵי עֲשֵׂה וְדָחֵי לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading in step 9 by showing it seems to cancel עשה דוחה לא תעשה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the great מצוה of building the מקדש does not override a simple לאו, then no עשה should override any לאו.

steps.title: שבת prohibitions are not considered special
steps.stepSummary: Someone might answer that שבת prohibitions are stricter. The גמרא rejects this, because the תנא applies the idea to ordinary prohibitions and sees no difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say שבת prohibitions are different because they are strict, that is wrong. The תנא speaks about prohibitions in general and does not raise this problem.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out, that שבת is stricter, and then shuts it down. This is the same move as step 4, repeated for the new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שבת were extra strict, we could say an עשה does not override שבת but does override other לאוין. The גמרא says the תנא does not treat שבת as special. He uses the same idea for ordinary prohibitions, so this escape does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
It is different
They are strict / severe
He is speaking about the general case

phrases.english: And if you say,
the prohibitions of שבת are different, because they are strict —
but the תנא is speaking about prohibitions in general,
and he does not raise any difficulty!
phrases.notes: He means the תנא sees no problem using this idea for ordinary prohibitions too, so שבת is not a special case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, שָׁאנֵי לָאוֵי דְּשַׁבָּת דַּחֲמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible defense against step 10 by repeating the logic of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that only שבת prohibitions resist being overridden
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא applies the principle to ordinary prohibitions, so שבת cannot be the reason.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a father's improper command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא again as proof for step 11. A son does not obey his father's order to become טמא or not to return a lost object, because everyone must honor הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: You might think that if a father tells his son 'become טמא' or 'do not return it,' the son should listen. The פסוק says: 'Each man shall fear his mother and his father, and keep My שבתות.' All of you must honor Me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא it already used in step 5. Here it is the proof that the תנא treats ordinary prohibitions the same way as שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Becoming טמא as a כהן and ignoring a lost object are ordinary לאוין, not שבת prohibitions. Yet the ברייתא learns them from a פסוק that speaks about שבת. This shows the תנא does not treat שבת as stricter than other prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: Become ritually impure
Do not return (the lost object)
The פָּסוּק teaches
All of you are obligated in My honor

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, יָכוֹל אָמַר לוֹ אָבִיו: הִיטַּמֵּא,
phrases.english: As it is taught: You might think, if his father told him: Become impure,
or told him: Do not return the lost object,
you might think he should listen to him —
so the verse says:
"Each man shall fear his mother and his father, etc." —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:3. The rest of the פסוק is "and keep My שבתות, I am ה'."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, יָכוֹל אָמַר לוֹ אָבִיו: הִיטַּמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 11's claim that the תנא speaks generally.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנא applies the principle to ordinary prohibitions, not only to שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on ויקרא 19:3 about a father commanding a transgression

steps.title: Driving the animal is only a הכשר מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers step 10. We cannot learn that an עשה never overrides a לאו, because driving the animal is only a preparation for the מצוה, not the מצוה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that we can push back: what about these cases, which are only a preparation for a מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the challenge from step 10 with the same answer it gave in step 6. The building case cannot teach a general rule, because driving the animal is only a הכשר מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule עשה דוחה לא תעשה works when the forbidden act is itself the מצוה. Driving an animal to bring building materials only helps prepare for the מצוה. So the building case says nothing about a real מצוה act, and the general rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to push back / refute
What about these (cases), which are different
A preparation that makes a מִצְוָה possible, not the מִצְוָה itself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying building the בית המקדש is not a מצוה. It is a real מצוה. Only the driving of the animal is a preparation, and that is why it does not override the לאו.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because one can refute it:
what about these cases, which are only a preparation for a מצוה?
phrases.notes: "These" means driving the animal to bring materials. That act only gets things ready for the building.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by repeating the distinction from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (הכשר מצוה vs. the מצוה itself)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The building case seemed to prove that no עשה overrides a לאו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case only shows that a הכשר מצוה does not override a לאו. A real מצוה act still can.

steps.title: Why not learn הכשר מצוה from the father case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need the building of the מקדש to teach that a הכשר מצוה does not override a לאו. We could already learn it from the case of honoring parents.
steps.simpleTranslation: A preparation for a מצוה: let me derive it from there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the same lesson is taught twice. If כיבוד אב already shows that a preparation does not override a לאו, why do we need the building case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 6, the father case was explained as a הכשר מצוה. Now the building case is explained the same way. So one of the two looks unnecessary, and the גמרא wants to know why the building case is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me derive it / I can get it
From there (the other case)
Honoring father and mother

phrases.english: A preparation for a מצוה: let me derive it from there!
phrases.notes: "There" is the case of honoring parents, where serving the father was also only a preparation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 13 by saying the building case is unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the building of the מקדש as a separate source
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same lesson about הכשר מצוה is already known from honoring parents, so a second source looks extra.

steps.title: Agreed, so why is the פסוק about the מקדש needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the lesson can indeed come from the father case. Then it asks what the פסוק "keep My שבתות and revere My מקדש" comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is indeed so. Then why do I need "Keep My שבתות and revere My מקדש"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with step 14 and then turns the question around. If the father case is enough, what is the פסוק about the מקדש for?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 7 used ויקרא 19:30 to teach that building does not override שבת. Now that this lesson comes from the father case, that פסוק seems to have no job. The גמרא needs to find another lesson for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so
Why do I need it?
Revere My Sanctuary

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
Then "You shall keep My Shabbatot and revere My Sanctuary"
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 14's point and then asks what the פסוק teaches.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lesson comes from the father case, the פסוק about the מקדש seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches what kind of awe the מקדש deserves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is needed for a different ברייתא. It teaches what kind of reverence we must have for the מקדש, by comparing it to keeping שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what is taught: You might think a person should fear the מקדש itself. The פסוק says: "Keep My שבתות and revere My מקדש." Keeping is said about שבת, and reverence is said about the מקדש. Just as the keeping said about שבת...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק a new job. It explains the correct kind of awe for the מקדש, and the comparison to שבת continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא worries that a person might fear the building itself, as if the building were what we worship. By placing שבת and the מקדש side by side, the פסוק sets up a comparison between them. The sentence is cut off here, and its ending is in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for
You might have thought
Keeping / guarding
Fear / reverence

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the פסוק about the מקדש is not extra. It teaches a separate law about the right kind of awe for the מקדש.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught:
You might think a person should fear the Temple itself,
so the verse says:
"You shall keep My Shabbatot
and revere My Sanctuary."
Keeping is said about Shabbat,
and reverence is said about the Temple.
Just as the keeping said about Shabbat —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by giving the פסוק a different purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to be extra, since its lesson comes from the father case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches the proper kind of reverence for the מקדש, through a comparison to שבת.
